raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year the same way I always do. My old man and me, we've worked these 14 mu for decades. Our son works in town so it's mostly the two of us, and at my age I can't do what I used to — I'll hire the combine for harvest like always.

For the wheat, I'll plant in early October after the maize comes off, same variety I've been using — my neighbor 王大姐 uses it too and it does alright. I buy one bag of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu and spread it before planting, then in spring around jointing I topdress about half a bag of urea per mu. That's how we've always done it. If the wheat looks yellow I might add a bit more urea, but usually it's fine. I'll water it three times from the well — once before winter, once at jointing, once at grain fill. Water costs money from the well so I don't do more unless it's really dry. For weeds I spray once in spring, the village agri-shop sells what everyone uses.

For the maize, right after wheat harvest in June we plant hybrid seed — you have to buy new every year, can't save it. It's a tight week, the neighbor's boy helps with the planter. I put compound fertilizer down with the seed, about one bag per mu, then topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage. Maize doesn't need much watering if the summer rains come, maybe once or twice if it's dry. Spray once for weeds, and if I see the corn borer worm I'll spray for that too.

I keep some wheat and cornmeal for the house — we eat our own grain. Rest I sell. Can't afford to experiment much, we need the income steady.
